card.name: Just before a foreign personal name
card.fires_on: The word right before a person's name, often a non-English one: a job title, a speech verb like says, or a partial surname. Seen in web text such as news, history and citations.

modes.label: Title before a name
modes.description: A role word such as architect, director or owner comes just before a person's name.
modes.example: commissioned<< architect>> Enrique Aberg to replace the cramped State

modes.label: Speech verb before a name
modes.description: A quote is followed by says or explains, then the speaker's name.
modes.example: "The software creates a 3D view from all sides for any time of the day or time of the year,"<< says>> Alexander Wollert, a scientist at

modes.label: Inside a surname
modes.description: The first part of a European surname in a citation or contact line, with the rest of the name still to come.
modes.example: Svensson E, Haaijer-Ruskamp FM, Lund<<borg>> CS.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward European, Slavic and Latin first names and surnames, and away from common English male names like James or Craig.
card.plain: It fires where a foreign-sounding person's name is about to appear, such as after a job title or says.
